name: Cheng Sanrong
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Kunshan Huguang Auto Harness Co. (沪光股份, SSE: 605333)
profile: Founded the forerunner of Huguang in Zhangpu town, Kunshan in 1988 at age 25, making wiring harnesses for excavators and bulldozers. Huguang became a Volkswagen A-grade supplier in 1999 and listed in Shanghai in 2020; it is now a leading Chinese auto wiring-harness maker with R&D in Germany, Korea, North America and a plant in Romania (2023).
interesting_fact: Huguang started with just a pair of scissors, a wire stripper and a wooden board; the stripper was its only power tool. Today it runs a 'lights-out' (dark) factory and anchors ~50 suppliers in Kunshan.
deep_cut_fact: A couplet in his reception room reads '心中有梦想，眼里有沪光' (A dream in the heart, Huguang in the eyes). He says his three dreams in turn were to become a '10,000-yuan household', to be a JV-brand supplier, and to build a lights-out factory. He has risen at 4:30am for decades.
notes: Hurun listing is shared with Jin Chengcheng (family). 'Huguang' = 沪光, Kunshan Huguang Auto Electric. Best route: company IR email / SSE Roadshow Center investor sessions. Quote: '风浪越大鱼越贵' (the bigger the waves, the pricier the fish).

name: Guo Junwei
profile: Guo Junwei (郭俊伟) is reported to be a brother of Kaisa Group founder Guo Yingcheng (Kwok Ying Shing); the Guo family co-founded the Shenzhen developer Kaisa in 1999. Reports say he transferred a 16.42% Kaisa stake held via the family trust to Guo Xiaoqun. He appeared on Hurun only 2009-2012; no current public role found.
interesting_fact: Kaisa, founded in Shenzhen in 1999 by the Guo brothers, grew into a Hong Kong-listed developer (HKEX: 1638) known for urban-renewal projects in Shenzhen.
notes: Very low public profile; little beyond family-trust shareholding reports. Kaisa has been in debt restructuring since 2021 (avoid as an angle). Not a good outreach target; any approach would have to go via Kaisa Group corporate channels.

name: Susan Hagedorn
current_role: Nurse practitioner, professor emerita (University of Colorado nursing), documentary filmmaker and philanthropist; Hagedorn family >10% holder in ScottsMiracle-Gro
profile: Eldest daughter of Miracle-Gro co-founder Horace Hagedorn; the family kept a large stake in ScottsMiracle-Gro after the 1995 Scotts merger. She built a career as a nurse practitioner and nursing educator (UMass Amherst BSN '77, Boston College MS, Colorado doctorate) and has produced 20+ films on nursing and social justice.
interesting_fact: In 2021 she gave UMass Amherst's Elaine Marieb College of Nursing $2 million to create a diversity and inclusion program, and received the UMass Alumni Association's Revolutionary Spirit Award.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 she co-founded Nurstory with the founders of the digital-storytelling movement StoryCenter, a project using nurses' personal stories in nursing education. Her films include 'The Berrigans: Devout and Dangerous' and 'Island Nurse'.
notes: Wealth is passive (family ScottsMiracle-Gro stake); not involved in company management. Her Wikipedia article is flagged as possibly AI-generated, so treat it with care; the UMass page is the solid source. No published personal contact found; a possible route is via her film/Nurstory work or UMass nursing college. Not an energy/data-center fit.

name: Cai Xiaoru
current_role: Founder and major (>5%) shareholder, Fuzhou Tatwah Smartech Co. (达华智能, SZSE: 002512); former chairman
profile: Cai Xiaoru (蔡小如) founded Tatwah Smartech in Zhongshan, Guangdong, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010 as a contactless IC card/RFID-tag maker. He then grew it by acquisitions into IoT, fintech and satellite-communications businesses. Chen Rongsheng is now chairman; Cai remains a top-10 shareholder per the 2025 annual report.
interesting_fact: Under Cai, Tatwah went from a pure contactless smart-card/RFID manufacturer to a serial acquirer: it bought Xindongwang (2013), then a string of IoT and internet-finance companies from 2015, earning him the nickname 'M&A madman' in the Chinese press.
notes: The emails belong to the board secretary and securities representative, as published in the 2025 annual report summary; they are company channels, not Cai's. He no longer runs the company, which now trades as 'ST达华' (special treatment). Some of his shares were judicially auctioned in 2021, so avoid wealth/control topics. Low public profile.

name: Wang Bingkun
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & General Manager, De Rucci Healthy Sleep Co. (慕思股份, SZSE: 001323)
profile: Born in 1972 in Houjie, Dongguan, a furniture hub, Wang started out distributing furniture brands. In 2004 he put in all his savings plus loans from relatives and friends to co-found the mattress brand De Rucci with Lin Jiyong. It became China's top-selling mattress brand, has 1,400+ stores and listed in Shenzhen in 2022.
interesting_fact: De Rucci opened 600+ stores in its first five years. In 2010 it opened what it calls China's first private 'healthy sleep' club, and it set up a German subsidiary in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: His epiphany came on a furniture-fair study trip to Europe: a bed in an Italian hotel felt 'like floating on water'. He flipped the mattress, saw a slatted 'rib-frame' base for the first time, and carried two bed sets home from Europe to study them.
notes: The IR email is the board secretary/securities office address in De Rucci's shareholder-meeting notices; the office is in the Securities Investment Dept., Houjie, Dongguan. Investor Q&A also runs through ir.p5w.net.

name: Liu Haiyan
profile: Hurun lists Liu Haiyan (刘海燕) as the owner of Continental Hope (大陆希望集团), the Chengdu-based group with electrical-equipment/energy businesses. That group was founded by Liu Yongyan, eldest of the four Liu brothers who started Hope Group. I could not find a public source that sets out her role or relationship there.
interesting_fact: Continental Hope comes from the original Hope Group that the four Liu brothers (Liu Yongyan, Liu Yongxing, Chen Yuxin/Liu Yongmei, Liu Yonghao) started in the 1980s. Liu Yongyan took the high-tech branch, which holds many energy and power patents.
notes: Identity not verified: web searches only turn up unrelated people named Liu Haiyan, and nothing ties her to Continental Hope beyond the Hurun list (2013-2026). She is probably a family member of the Liu Yongyan branch; do not assume this. Extremely low profile; any approach would go via Continental Hope Group corporate channels.

name: Xu Xiong
current_role: Founder and former chairman/actual controller, Eastern Pioneer Driving School (东方时尚, SSE: 603377); no current executive role
profile: Xu Xiong (徐雄) founded Beijing's Eastern Pioneer Driving School, which grew into one of China's largest driving-training companies and listed in Shanghai in 2016 as China's first A-share driving school; it later expanded into flight training. His holding company controls ~65% via Eastern Pioneer Investment. In 2023 he was arrested and his brother took over as chairman.
interesting_fact: Eastern Pioneer was the first driving school to list on China's A-share market (2016).
notes: Not a viable outreach target: in Sept 2023 the company announced Xu had been arrested on suspicion of securities-market manipulation (jiemian 10337622). The company is now 'ST东时' and loss-making. Do not use this as a hook.

name: Guo Li
current_role: Reported CFO / early partner, CDH Investments (鼎晖投资)
profile: Guo Li (郭力) appears on Hurun (2015-2021) as a CDH Investments shareholder. Aggregator profiles describe a Ms. Guo Li who joined CDH in its founding year (2002) and serves as CFO of CDH Investments Management (HK). She previously worked at Arthur Andersen (1997-2001), is a CPA and graduated from the Central University of Finance and Economics.
interesting_fact: CDH grew out of the direct-investment department of China International Capital Corp (CICC). It was spun out in 2002 by six founders led by Wu Shangzhi and Jiao Zhen, with GIC, China Investment Guarantee and Zurich Capital, and became one of China's largest PE firms.
notes: Identity only moderately confirmed: the CFO background comes from data aggregators (mergr.com, marketscreener), not an official CDH page. Very low profile. Any approach would go through CDH corporate channels (cdhfund.com).

name: Su Da
current_role: General Manager, Jiangsu Leili Motor Co. (江苏雷利, SZSE: 300660)
profile: Su Da (苏达) runs Changzhou-based Jiangsu Leili Motor, the micro-motor maker his father Su Jianguo founded in 1993; its first product was an air-conditioner motor. He has steered Leili from ~90% home-appliance revenue (pre-2017 IPO) into EV motors, medical micro-motors (via Dingzhi Tech) and now robotics/embodied-AI components such as coreless motors and dexterous hands.
interesting_fact: Roughly one in three air conditioners and one in five washing machines worldwide uses a Leili motor. Its high-end motors now reach 100,000 rpm.
deep_cut_fact: Leili controls Anhui Zhongke Lingxi, a USTC-incubated dexterous-robot-hand maker. Su splits embodied-AI commercialisation into three tiers: service, then industrial/commercial, then elder care. He predicts service robots scale first and end up with an EV-like market structure (Paper, July 2026).
notes: Emails are for the board secretary (Yin Chenglong) and the securities representative, as published in Leili's reports. Su speaks to media ('Vibrant China' tour 2026), so he is relatively accessible. Good robotics/electrification angle. Listing shared with Su Jianguo.

name: Chen Zhuoxiong
current_role: Former executive/non-executive director, Agile Group Holdings (雅居乐, HKEX: 3383); reportedly stepped down April 2026
profile: Chen Zhuoxiong (陈卓雄) is one of the Chen brothers (with chairman Chen Zhuolin) who founded Guangdong property developer Agile in Zhongshan in the 1990s; it listed in Hong Kong in 2005. He oversaw strategy for Agile's property-services arm A-Living and its environmental-protection group, and was reported to have resigned as a non-executive director on 1 April 2026.
interesting_fact: Beyond homebuilding, Agile built a property-management platform (A-Living) and an environmental-protection business (Yacheng Ecological), both of which Chen was responsible for strategically.
notes: Agile is in offshore debt restructuring and faces winding-up petitions, so avoid the topic. The April 2026 resignation comes from a lixinger summary and should be checked on HKEX. Listing is shared with Lu Liqing. Low profile; best route is Agile IR.

name: Chen Wenpei
current_role: Chairman, SCAS Investment Group Co. Ltd. (per MarketScreener; unverified)
profile: Chen Wenpei (陈文沛) appears on Hurun (2011-2021) with wealth from 'SCAS', an investment group. MarketScreener lists Chen WenPei as chairman of SCAS Investment Group and from Dec 2019 a director of ChongHerr Investments, an Australian company that holds sandstone mining leases in Helidon, Queensland. No official SCAS source was found.
interesting_fact: He is linked to ChongHerr Investments, which mines and exports Helidon Sandstone from Queensland. Helidon sandstone is a historic building stone used in many Australian landmarks.
notes: Identity is only weakly confirmed through a single data aggregator, so check that it is the same person before any outreach. Very low public profile.

name: Yu Shuixiang
profile: Hurun China (2020-2021) lists Yu Shuixiang (俞水祥) with wealth from 'Sunriver' (infrastructure, real estate). Searches found no public profile for anyone of this name, and nothing linking it to the Sunriver/Xiangsheng-related groups (Zhejiang Sunriver Culture Tourism, SH 600576; Sunriver Holding Group).
notes: Could not identify. 'Sunriver' is the English name used by Xiangsheng (祥生)-linked groups, which have had serious debt problems since 2025, so avoid that topic. Skip unless the journalist can supply more identifying detail.

name: Yang Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and former chairman/actual controller, Shanghai New Culture Media Group (新文化, SZSE: 300336); no current role found
profile: Yang Zhenhua (杨震华) founded Shanghai New Culture Media (est. Dec 2004), a film/TV drama investment, production and distribution company that listed on ChiNext in 2012. Filings from 2020 call him the 'former actual controller' with ~10.5% of shares, and by 2024 the company had a different chairman.
interesting_fact: New Culture Media was one of the private TV-drama production houses that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board soon after it launched.
notes: Hurun listing (2014-2017) is shared with Yang Lu. He has given up control and has been cutting his stake (2022 reduction plan), and the company now trades with a modified ticker prefix. Low profile; no published contact.
